name: Tencent Cloud
tagline: China-based enterprise cloud platform with Lighthouse VPS for simple website hosting
description: Tencent Cloud is a large China-based enterprise cloud platform; this listing covers its Lighthouse and CVM virtual machine products for basic website hosting only.
about: Tencent Cloud is one of China's largest cloud computing providers, offering a vast enterprise catalog spanning AI, gaming infrastructure, CDN, databases and more. This listing does not attempt to cover that whole catalog — it's scoped narrowly to two products relevant to website hosting: Cloud Virtual Machine (CVM), Tencent's general-purpose VPS line, and Lighthouse, a simplified, pre-configured VPS aimed at small sites and individual developers.

Lighthouse's entry plan runs from roughly $4/month for 1 vCPU, 1GB RAM, 50GB SSD and 1TB of monthly transfer, billed as a fixed-term VPS rather than hourly. Tencent regularly discounts new-customer sign-up terms well below that (promotional listings as low as $1.68/month for a short first term), so check the live checkout price against the standard renewal rate before committing. New users of CVM or Lighthouse are also eligible for a 3-month free trial (2 vCPU/2GB for Lighthouse, or CVM S5 2 vCPU/4GB) — available once per account and not to previous purchasers of either product.

Because Tencent Cloud is headquartered in and optimized for the Chinese market, expect the best latency and support experience for sites primarily serving mainland China. International account sign-up requires real-name identity verification, and the self-serve international console has less English-language documentation than competitors like DigitalOcean or Vultr.
policies: Tencent Cloud's refund and cancellation terms vary by product and billing mode (prepaid vs. pay-as-you-go); prepaid VPS terms are generally non-refundable once provisioned except where required by local consumer law, so review the specific refund policy on the order page before purchasing.

New-account sign-up requires real-name verification (identity or business documentation) before some services, including CVM and Lighthouse, can be activated — factor this into setup time if you're evaluating it for the first time.
